rules.description: Working Time Directive Art. 7: at least four weeks paid annual leave; no payment in lieu except on termination

source.title: Directive 2003/88/EC concerning certain aspects of the organisation of working time (EUR-Lex)

versions.notes: Art. 7(1) "paid annual leave of at least four weeks"; Art. 7(2) allowance in lieu only where the employment relationship is terminated. Art. 28: entry into force 2 August 2004.

rules.description: Working Time Directive Art. 6 + Art. 16(b): 48-hour average week including overtime, reference period up to 4 months

source.title: Directive 2003/88/EC concerning certain aspects of the organisation of working time (EUR-Lex)

versions.notes: Art. 6(b): average working time for each seven-day period, including overtime, does not exceed 48 hours. Art. 16(b): reference period not exceeding four months (derogations in Arts. 17-19 not modelled).

rules.description: Working Time Directive Art. 3: 11 consecutive hours per 24-hour period

source.title: Directive 2003/88/EC concerning certain aspects of the organisation of working time (EUR-Lex)

rules.description: Working Time Directive Art. 5 + Art. 16(a): 24 hours uninterrupted plus the 11 hours daily rest per 7-day period; reference period up to 14 days

source.title: Directive 2003/88/EC concerning certain aspects of the organisation of working time (EUR-Lex)

versions.notes: Art. 5: minimum uninterrupted rest of 24 hours plus the 11 hours daily rest per seven-day period; a minimum of 24 hours may apply if justified by objective, technical or work-organisation conditions. Art. 16(a): reference period not exceeding 14 days.

rules.description: Working Time Directive Art. 4: rest break where the working day is longer than six hours

source.title: Directive 2003/88/EC concerning certain aspects of the organisation of working time (EUR-Lex)

versions.notes: Art. 4: duration and terms laid down in collective agreements or, failing that, national legislation.

rules.description: CJEU C-55/18 (CCOO): Member States must require employers to set up an objective, reliable and accessible system measuring daily working time

value.basis: CJEU C-55/18 reading Arts. 3, 5, 6 WTD with Art. 31(2) Charter and Directive 89/391/EEC

source.title: CJEU judgment of 14 May 2019, CCOO v Deutsche Bank SAE, C-55/18 (EUR-Lex)

versions.notes: Judgment of 14 May 2019 (Grand Chamber): the Directive precludes national law that does not require employers to set up a system enabling the duration of time worked each day by each worker to be measured. Obligation applies to Member States; employer-level obligation depends on national implementation (see member-state packs).

rules.description: Pay Transparency Directive (EU) 2023/970: transposition deadline and gender pay gap reporting thresholds

definitions.genderPayGap: difference in average pay levels between female and male workers, as a percentage of the average pay level of male workers
definitions.medianGenderPayGap: difference between the median pay level of female and of male workers, as a percentage of the median pay level of male workers
definitions.quartilePayBand: each of four equal groups of workers divided according to their pay levels, from the lowest to the highest
definitions.categoryOfWorkers: workers performing the same work or work of equal value, grouped in a non-arbitrary manner on objective gender-neutral criteria (Art. 4(4))

versions.notes: Art. 9(2): 250+ workers by 7 June 2027 and every year thereafter; Art. 9(3): 150-249 by 7 June 2027 and every three years; Art. 9(4): 100-149 by 7 June 2031 and every three years; each report concerns the previous calendar year. Art. 34(1): transposition by 7 June 2026. Directive done at Strasbourg 10 May 2023. Other Articles (pay transparency before employment, right to information, joint pay assessment) not modelled. Phase 5 (verified 2026-10-18 on EUR-Lex): Art. 3(1)(b) "pay level" = gross annual pay and the corresponding gross hourly pay; (c) gender pay gap and (e) median gender pay gap as a percentage of the male figure; (f) quartile pay band; (h) category of workers; Art. 9(1)(a)-(g) indicators; Art. 10(1) joint pay assessment where a difference of at least 5% in any category of workers is not justified on objective, gender-neutral criteria and not remedied within six months of the submission of the pay reporting.

coverage.notes: EU minimums only; member-state packs override. No holidays at EU level.
